goal: Compare original GSD, GSD2, and Azoth for future Azoth architecture research
refresh_summary: First durable capture of the GSD, GSD2, and Azoth comparison. This capsule preserves the static source-level findings, strategic judgment, source trail, and follow-up research threads so future sessions can refresh or deepen the comparison without rebuilding it from chat history.
limitations: GSD and GSD2 findings are based on primary GitHub source inspection and sidecar read-only analysis, not local clone execution or test runs.
GSD2 is under active development; package version, runtime state design, model routing, and extension surfaces should be refreshed before implementation decisions.
Popularity signals such as current stars or package downloads were not used as evidence because they were not fetched during this session.
Azoth findings reflect the local root-azoth checkout at capture time and may drift as gates, pipelines, and autonomous-auto work continue.
This capsule is research evidence only. It does not authorize implementation, migration, governance mutation, or adoption of GSD/GSD2 runtime patterns.

questions.question: Can this GSD/GSD2/Azoth comparison capsule be reused for future architecture, proposal, or research sessions?
What is the strongest source-backed comparison between original GSD, GSD2, and Azoth for future Azoth architecture research?

thesis: Original GSD is a strong prompt/workflow kit and is better than Azoth at approachable app-building ergonomics, but weaker at mechanically governed truth. GSD2 is materially ahead of Azoth as a standalone autonomous coding runtime. Azoth remains stronger as a repo-native governance substrate with explicit gates, ledgers, planning banks, typed staged boundaries, and cross-tool generated manifests.

executive_judgment.original_gsd: Not better than Azoth overall. Better for low-friction project workflow, phase planning, wave execution, and UAT-style shipping momentum; weaker for fail-closed governance and auditable approval state.
executive_judgment.gsd2: Better than Azoth as a runtime execution engine. It owns sessions, DB-backed state, worker leases, dispatch claims, worktrees, metrics, crash recovery, extensions, and model routing.
executive_judgment.azoth: Better than both for governed repo-native truth: approval boundaries, run-ledger evidence, planning-bank readiness, staged subagent contracts, closeout discipline, and multi-platform generated surfaces.
executive_judgment.strategic_recommendation: Borrow GSD2 runtime primitives underneath Azoth, but keep Azoth gates, planning banks, route state, and ledgers as the authoritative governance layer.

comparison_matrix.finding: GSD2 owns execution as a TypeScript/Pi runtime. Original GSD and Azoth rely more on existing coding-tool runtimes.
GSD provides smoother project-start, phase-plan, execute, and verify flows. Azoth is more explicit but more cognitively heavy.
Azoth's gates, run ledger, closeout, planning banks, and typed staged summaries are more naturally repo-auditable.
GSD2 has the strongest runtime state model, while Azoth has the stronger governance-state model.
GSD2's fresh-session-per-dispatch model is the strongest runtime answer to context decay; Azoth's typed boundaries are stronger as audit artifacts.

package_identity.description: Meta-prompting, context engineering, and spec-driven development system for Claude Code, OpenCode, Gemini, and Codex.

strengths: Clear .planning artifact model with PROJECT, config, research, requirements, roadmap, state, plans, summaries, and verification.
Strong practical workflow set: new-project, plan-phase, execute-phase, autonomous, execute-plan, verify-work, and map-codebase.
Wave execution doctrine and broad subagent catalog for executor, verifier, planner, researcher, plan-checker, debugger, codebase-mapper, integration-checker, UI, and audit roles.
Good context-engineering posture: phase-scoped context, truncation, state-driven loading, and command wrappers.
Real security utilities for path traversal, prompt injection, shell argument validation, JSON safety, prompt structure validation, and entropy anomaly checks.
weaknesses_vs_azoth: Several controls are prompt-enforced, advisory, or soft rather than fail-closed.
Runtime fallbacks can collapse subagent boundaries into sequential or inline execution.
Code review and some gates are designed not to block execution, which preserves momentum but weakens governed assurance.
Human-gate and approval state are less durable and less mechanically auditable than Azoth's gate plus run-ledger model.

package_identity.description: Standalone GSD coding agent built on Pi SDK with CLI, headless, MCP, extension, native-engine, and editor surfaces.

strengths: Standalone TypeScript/Pi agent runtime rather than a prompt-only layer.
DB-authoritative runtime state with workers, leases, unit dispatches, command queue, runtime KV, assessments, tasks, gates, evidence, memories, and artifacts.
Fresh agent session per dispatch to reduce context degradation.
Rule-driven auto-dispatch over planning, execution, validation, UAT, completion, escalation, and stop states.
First-class milestone worktrees with sync, squash merge, conflict handling, cleanup, and branch identity checks.
Crash recovery from DB workers, dispatches, runtime KV, stale heartbeats, and OS PID checks.
Per-unit token and cost metrics, model routing, budget pressure handling, provider/tool filtering, and fallback logic.
Broad extension system with component schemas for skills, agents, tool allow/deny lists, timeouts, isolation, merge strategy, and output schemas.
weaknesses_vs_azoth: More runtime complexity: SQLite DB, migrations, locks, workers, leases, native packages, projections, extension installs, and recovery paths.
Less naturally audit-portable because important truth lives in local runtime DB and projections rather than versioned repo-native governance artifacts.
Single-host SQLite/WAL model is powerful locally but not a distributed coordination model.
Supply-chain and operational surface is larger due to extension installation and provider/runtime breadth.
Product culture favors shipping fast and fixing fast; Azoth is more conservative about explicit human gates and staged provenance.

strengths: Repo-native governance kernel with session-gate, scope-gate, pipeline-gate, run-ledger, write claims, completion evidence, and closeout.
Planning banks separate evidence, design state, initiative readiness, and executable roadmap/spec hydration.
Generated multi-platform command, skill, agent, and IDE-rule surfaces through azoth-deploy.
Typed subagent routing and stage summaries make fresh-context and review-independence boundaries auditable.
Codex model selector records policy, tier, effort, fallback reason, confidence, and signal metadata.
Closeout is a governed lifecycle operation, not only a narrative summary.
weaknesses_vs_gsd_family: Higher operator cognitive load and more ceremony for small implementation slices.
Less productized standalone runtime: no GSD2-equivalent DB worker/lease harness, TUI, extension marketplace, or built-in cost dashboard.
More local-state fragility around gitignored gates and ledgers across worktrees.
Dynamic-full-auto in Codex remains constrained by host runtime and network limitations.

candidate_azoth_followups.description: Research whether Azoth should add a DB or structured execution-ledger layer for worker leases, dispatch claims, stale-heartbeat recovery, and per-unit metrics while keeping repo-native governance as authority.
Prototype or design how Azoth could require fresh-context execution units for selected stages without losing run-ledger and stage-summary traceability.
Compare GSD/GSD2 operator UX against Azoth's gate-heavy workflow and design a compact operator surface that preserves safety without exposing every mechanism every time.
Evaluate whether original GSD's new-project, UAT, map-codebase, and verify-work ergonomics should inspire Azoth command or playbook improvements.
Define which GSD2-style DB/runtime fields should be projected into repo-native Azoth artifacts for audit, replay, and cross-tool continuity.

sidecar_agents.summary: Found GSD to be a practical multi-runtime workflow kit with rich .planning artifacts, wave execution, broad subagent roles, SDK-backed context, and real security utilities; main gap is enforcement depth.
Found GSD2 to be a standalone TypeScript/Pi runtime with DB-first state, worker leases, unit dispatches, worktrees, fresh sessions, model routing, metrics, crash recovery, and extensions.

Found Azoth to be a repo-native governance/workflow kernel with gates, ledgers, planning banks, generated multi-platform surfaces, typed subagent boundaries, model selector traces, and closeout discipline.
